concept_options.title: How Fast Can Anything Go? - Speed Ladder (style of video 13)
concept_options.hook: You walk at about five kilometres an hour. A cheetah sprints at about a hundred. A diving falcon hits nearly four hundred.
concept_options.visual_approach: REUSED ENGINE 'Black-Body' (video 13's log-scale ladder, zeros counter, window plates and tags), re-dressed as 'Speed Ladder': a night-ink sky with a vertical log-scale rail in km/h from 1 to 10^9; a single glowing marker climbs rung by rung (WALK 5 · CHEETAH ~100 · FALCON ~390 · SOUND 1,235 · EARTH 107,000 · PARKER 692,000 · LIGHT 1,079,252,849) with a ZEROS counter (0 -> 9) and speed streaks whose length grows with the log of speed. The top of the rail is a hard line 'c'. The marker can approach it but never touch it: in the close, an LHC readout fills nines '99.9999991 %' while the gap shrinks and stays. Windows show tagged AI stills (cheetah, falcon, Parker Solar Probe near the Sun). Colour is NOT a temperature here: one white-cyan accent for the marker, steel for the rail.
concept_options.core_message: You're already fast; our fastest machine is a crawl next to light; and light speed is a wall nothing with mass can reach.
concept_options.cta: Spoken finished close: 'Close. But never all the way.' Caption: 'What's the fastest thing you've ridden?'
concept_options.tone: curious, building, then a quiet deadpan close
concept_options.why_this_works: Completes the 'How X can it get' set (loud, cold, hot) with the same log-ladder grammar viewers already know, reusing video 13's ladder and counter code. The 'you're doing 100,000 km/h right now' beat puts the viewer on the scale. Risk: same engine as video 13 - re-dressed (no black-body colour, white-cyan marker, speed streaks) and the twist is different (a wall, not a fray).

taste_profile.design_read: Youth science short: a calm climb up one speed ladder, from walking to light, ending at a wall that never moves.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Night ink sky, steel rail, ONE white-cyan accent for the marker; no temperature colours; red only for 'c' (the wall).
taste_profile.layout_variation: Log rail + marker, zeros counter, window plates, the LHC nines readout.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Numbers from the brief only; AI stills as short tagged inserts.
anti_patterns: 'the falcon is the fastest animal' as fact without the dive caveat
quality_gates: Every rung's number matches the brief
